prompt.en: A learner builds a source map before reviewing station duties. Which ordering is the most defensible from broad authority toward individual operating records?

text.en: Certificate folder, department name, service definition, broad statute
Broad statute, regulations that define the service, ISED station standards, certificate and call-sign records
Club handbook, call-sign preference, examiner invoice, broad statute
Exam accommodation note, station log, service definition, department name

explanation.en: The lesson groups sources from general legal authority to operating standards and finally to the individual certificate and call-sign records that identify the operator.

prompt.en: Which study habit would NOT help keep current fee rules accurate?

text.en: Separating an ISED office exam from an accredited examiner's cost recovery
Checking whether a call-sign action is address-related or voluntary
Using the current bank rather than a remembered club-story amount
Combining every certificate, call-sign, and exam situation into one universal price rule

explanation.en: The bank treats different services differently. A single universal price rule would blur first certificates, address-related prefix replacement, voluntary call-sign changes, ISED office exams, and examiner cost recovery.

prompt.en: A drill planner says, 'We can use a fake emergency word if we immediately explain that it was a scenario.' What is the error in that procedure?

text.en: A later explanation does not change the nature of transmitting false emergency information.
Practice traffic is forbidden even when no emergency word is used.
Only club officers are allowed to label an exercise as practice traffic.
False wording becomes acceptable whenever a net control station is listening.

explanation.en: The safe procedure is to identify exercise traffic without sending a false distress or false emergency claim in the first place.
